subject: Runbook: dedicated capacity sizing & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@clearlane.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Runbook: dedicated capacity sizing & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated correctly:

Recap of the call:
- ClearLane is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for production. Primary drivers: latency (<150ms p50), predictable unit cost, and data residency for a subset of PII flows.
- Workload profile: mainly generative assistant + reranking for search; some batch scoring jobs overnight.
- Candidate model family mentioned: an OSS 70B (8k context) quantized variant.

What we need from you to finalize a Dedicated proposal (short list):
1) TPS targets: what is your average TPS and expected peak TPS (15–60 minute windows)?
2) Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions/requests during peak and baseline.
3) Token mix: average prompt length, average generated tokens, percentage of long-context queries.
4) SLA/availability expectations and whether you require an SLA-backed plan or self-service Reserved capacity.
5) Any procurement timing or lead-time constraints we should be aware of.

I've attached our Draft Dedicated Playbook (redwood-dedicated-playbook-v1.pdf) — it includes rough mapping of model families to GPU tiers and an example autoscale policy. If you can reply with the items above (or attach a forecast), we’ll run a quick sizing exercise and return a recommended node mix (GPU types, reserved counts, autoscale thresholds) within 48 business hours.

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with TPS/concurrency/token mix (see bullets above).
- We deliver a sizing runbook and recommended procurement SKUs.
- Optional follow-up call with Marcus (in infra) to walk through the runbook.

Would Tuesday morning PST (11/16) work for a 30-min sizing walkthrough?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

redwood.ai

From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@clearlane.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Runbook: dedicated capacity sizing & next steps

Hi Tessa —

Appreciate the recap, that aligns with our internal notes. See answers below and I attached our FY27 traffic forecast.

1) TPS targets:
- Baseline (avg sustained during business hours): ~1,200 TPS
- Peak windows (30–60min): up to ~2,500 TPS during marketing-driven bursts

2) Concurrency:
- Typical concurrent sessions during peak: ~350–450 (mostly short, chat-style requests)

3) Token mix:
- 85% of calls: prompt ~300 tokens, generation ~80–150 tokens
- 15% of calls: long-context sessions (user history + doc context), up to 2,000 tokens input, generation ~300–500 tokens
- Overall average total tokens per request: ~420

4) SLA: We’d prefer a Managed Dedicated plan with a 99.9% SLA for production-critical traffic. For non-sensitive batch scoring we can use a lower tier.

5) Procurement/lead time: Procurement window ~6–8 weeks. We need final pricing and SKUs by end of November to align with budget cycles.

Model: we plan to use an OSS 70B quantized (8k context). We are open to Redwood suggestions on model variants for cost vs latency.

Attachment: clearlane_mau_forecast.xlsx (XLSX, 320KB)

Quick question: given our token mix and peaks, do you recommend H100 or A100 for sustained cost-efficiency? Also curious if Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for long-context sessions to reduce compute on repeated context.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Platform | ClearLane AI
alex.wu@clearlane.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@clearlane.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Runbook: dedicated capacity sizing & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the detailed numbers — very helpful. High-level guidance based on the profile you provided:

GPU recommendation: H100 preferred for your peak/quantized 70B workload if low p50 latency is important and you expect sustained bursts. H100 gives better perf for attention-heavy models and larger batch headroom; it also handles 8-bit quantized execution with higher throughput. A100 80GB is still a strong choice for cost-sensitive steady workloads but you may need more nodes to hit your peak TPS.

Sizing notes (initial):
- Baseline (1,200 TPS): estimated 6–8 H100 reserved instances (with continuous batching & prefix caching enabled)
- Peak buffer (2,500 TPS): additional burst pool of 4–6 H100 GPU capacity (autoscale policy to add/remove within 5–10 min)
- Concurrency: plan for 400 logical concurrent sessions; we recommend routing/queueing rules to prioritize low-latency trafﬁc over batch scoring.
- Token mix: enable KV/prefix caching for the 15% long-context sessions — this will materially reduce per-request compute if history is repeated. We can set cache TTL per-session and use warm-start for commonly accessed docs.

Deliverables we’ll produce for you by Monday EOD (based on your forecast):
- Node mix spreadsheet (H100 vs A100 candidate counts) — see attached h100-vs-a100-tps-matrix.csv
- Example autoscale policy + estimated monthly cost delta for Dedicated managed plan
- Migration runbook for moving sensitive flows into a VPC/private control plane

Questions for you to confirm:
- Do you require all traffic to be routed through VPC/private control plane or only a subset (PII flows)?
- Can you share a short list of example long-context queries (we’ll use these to validate cache hit expectations)?

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min sizing walkthrough next week to finalize reserved counts and procurement SKUs.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
